title: Taliesin: The Shape-Shifter
subtitle: Chased through a dozen forms — the poet who becomes everything he sings

narrativeBlocks.title: The three drops of wisdom
narrativeBlocks.body: The witch Cerridwen brews a cauldron of wisdom for her ugly son — three drops will grant all knowledge. Her servant-boy Gwion stirs it, and the drops splash on his thumb instead.

narrativeBlocks.title: Instant omniscience
narrativeBlocks.body: The moment the drops touch his tongue, Gwion knows everything — including that Cerridwen will kill him. He flees by changing shape: a hare, a fish, a bird, a grain of wheat.

narrativeBlocks.title: The chase that can't end
narrativeBlocks.body: Cerridwen pursues as a greyhound, an otter, a hawk — and finally as a hen she swallows the wheat-grain that is Gwion. She thinks the chase is done.

narrativeBlocks.title: Born again as Taliesin
narrativeBlocks.body: But swallowing him makes her pregnant — nine months later she births a shining infant and, unable to kill it, casts him into the sea. Rescued from the weir, he grows into Taliesin, the greatest of bards.

narrativeBlocks.title: Poetry as transformation
narrativeBlocks.body: Taliesin's story is the poet's myth of itself: the bard claims to have BEEN everything — the hunt, the grain, the child in the sea. Imagination lets a man wear every shape; that is what the tale says poetry is.
